app_store.name: wireX Network Simulator
app_store.subtitle: Build networks in your browser
app_store.promotional_text: A browser-based network engineering lab: build topologies, run IOS-style CLI, watch layered packets travel, and practice classroom topics in English, Arabic, or Kurdish.
app_store.description:
wireX is a browser-native network engineering lab for students and instructors.

Build a topology with routers, switches, servers, PCs, laptops, wireless devices, IP phones, and an ASA security appliance. Connect them with the right cable, manage real chassis views with power interlocks, insert expansion modules, and configure everything through an authentic IOS-style command line with tab completion, abbreviations, and context help.

What you get:
- Logical workspace with pan, zoom, group selection, sticky notes, and zone boxes
- Physical chassis views for 15 device families with power interlocks and modular bays
- Independent device windows you can tile side by side
- Realtime and simulation modes with animated packet envelopes and layer-by-layer PDU inspection
- DHCP with pools, leases, reservations, relay, conflicts, and renewal timers
- VLANs, trunks, STP with per-VLAN states, EtherChannel, and HSRP failover
- OSPF and RIPv2 routing with learned routes, withdrawal, and failover
- ACL filtering, NAT/PAT on ASA with ASDM-style management, and GRE tunnels with keepalives
- Desktop apps: IP configuration, command prompt, web browser, email, SNMP manager, phone GUI
- Built-in diagnostic engine that names the exact fault and the corrective commands

Students can practice on six guided campus lessons with automatic grading of the live network state. The interface is fully localized in English, Arabic, and Central Kurdish (Sorani) with right-to-left layout while terminal output stays left-to-right.

Open supported .pkt topology files, export your work, and keep everything saved locally in the browser. Runs in any modern browser on desktop, Chromebook, and tablet. Completely free for students and instructors — no installer, no account, no license key, and no trial limits.
app_store.whats_new: Packet queues now scale to large campus labs (up to 4,096 in-flight frames), so dozens of simultaneous first-use pings complete on a 300-link topology. Email now speaks a command-level ESMTP/POP3 subset across simulated TCP, and the packet inspector warns when credentials appear without TLS. Smarter diagnostics, Arabic and Kurdish completion packs, and instructor activity authoring with live grading.

google_play.full_description:
wireX is a browser-native network engineering lab for students and instructors.

Build a topology with routers, switches, servers, PCs, laptops, wireless devices, IP phones, and an ASA security appliance. Connect them with the right cable, manage real chassis hardware with power interlocks and modular expansion bays, then configure everything through an authentic IOS-style CLI with help, tab completion, and abbreviations.

Practice core classroom topics end to end:
- Logical canvas: pan, zoom, marquee selection, notes, and zone boxes
- Physical chassis: front, rear, and side views for 15 device families
- Simulation: realtime and step modes with animated envelopes and full OSI-layer inspection
- Switching: VLANs, 802.1Q trunks, STP timers and port states, EtherChannel, MAC aging
- Routing: connected, static, OSPF, RIPv2, HSRP failover, relayed DHCP, route-based DNS
- Services: DHCP DORA with leases and reservations, DNS lookup, HTTP over routed TCP, TFTP, NTP, SNMP queries
- Email: ESMTP submission and POP3 retrieval and deletion over simulated TCP
- Security: standard and extended ACLs, NAT/PAT with stateful inspection, GRE tunnels with keepalives
- Telephony: CME configuration with a live IP phone GUI for dialing, ringing, and hold

A built-in diagnostics engine reads the live topology, tells you which interface or configuration is wrong, and hands you the corrective commands. Six guided campus lessons grade your actual network state, not your typing.

Fully localized in English, Arabic, and Central Kurdish (Sorani) with right-to-left layout and left-to-right technical terminals. Open supported .pkt topology files and save locally. Runs on any modern browser. Completely free — no installer, no account, no license key, and no trial limits.
